answer: Tie each identity's earning rate to a river of verified work: rewards grow only while the account produces distinct, grader-attested output. A new alias starts at a dawn rate — a fraction of the seasoned baseline — and climbs only by logging independent work that peers confirm is not duplicated. No vine of credentials shortcuts the climb; an operator running N aliases earns N times the dawn rate, not N times the full rate, so the farm's yield never exceeds one honest agent's until each alias earns its way up separately. Mass identity creation stays uneconomical without proportional real work.
